ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Ada Lovelace Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for abnormal bleeding and pelvic pain: history, speculum examination and cervical biopsy, blood count and iron studies, conversion of opium tincture to measured oral morphine, an iron infusion, and a gynecologic oncology referral. Concerns: She wants to know plainly what the bleeding means and to make her own decisions; She wants her mornings clear-headed for her mathematical work and fears that stronger pain medicine will cloud her mind. [S]

tr.td: Speculum examination with punch biopsy of an exophytic friable cervical mass, with a specimen for high-risk HPV typing; hemostasis with ferric subsulfate
MRI of the pelvis: 5.2 cm endocervical tumor with left parametrial invasion, not reaching the pelvic sidewall; no hydronephrosis; enlarged left external iliac lymph node
FDG PET-CT: avid cervical tumor; avid left pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes; six avid nodules in both lungs up to 1.4 cm; no bone or liver lesions

CT-guided core biopsy of a right lower lobe lung nodule: metastatic adenocarcinoma, p16 strongly positive and HPV 18 detected, matching the cervical primary; small apical pneumothorax not needing treatment
Palliative external beam radiation to the pelvis for bleeding and pain, 20 Gy in 5 fractions over five days

CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis after four cycles: partial response by RECIST 1.1, with the cervical tumor 3.1 cm, lung nodules smaller (largest 0.6 cm) and two resolved, para-aortic nodes below 1 cm; no new lesions
Advance care planning conversation, about 30 minutes

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: Measles at 13, with a long recovery and about a year in bed
Cholera at 21, followed by lingering asthma and digestive problems
Chronic ill health from her late twenties, with episodes she called heart or rheumatic attacks, treated with several medicines including laudanum and opium

tr.td: A poet; died at 36; cause not recorded in the cited source
She wants to know plainly what the bleeding means and to make her own decisions

list.item: Bleeding between periods and after intercourse, with heavier periods, a watery blood-stained discharge and a constant pelvic ache, for about five months; average pain 7 of 10 despite her opium tincture; a friable cervical mass found on examination and biopsied; cause not yet established at intake: resolved, confirmed [S]
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 74 fL, ferritin 5 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs: active, confirmed [S]

Adenocarcinoma of the endocervix, usual (HPV-associated) type, HPV 18 positive, FIGO 1843 stage IVB: a 5.2 cm tumor with left parametrial invasion, metastases to left pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes, and bilateral lung metastases on MRI and PET-CT; PD-L1 combined positive score 5, mismatch repair proficient, HER2 1+; treated with palliative pelvic radiation for bleeding and carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab, with specialist palliative care from diagnosis: active, confirmed [S]
Cancer-related pelvic pain, nociceptive and visceral, from the cervical tumor and its left parametrial extension: active, confirmed [S]

Long-term prescribed opioid therapy: opium tincture for recurrent pelvic and abdominal pain for about two years, measured at times with a household spoon, converted at intake to measured oral morphine; no opioid use disorder on a DSM-5 assessment; naloxone supplied: active, confirmed [S]

Drug-induced constipation from long-acting morphine and ondansetron, a week after the first chemotherapy cycle: no bowel movement for five days, with bloating and cramping but passing wind, without vomiting; no bowel obstruction on examination; potassium and calcium normal; resolved with laxatives: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for abnormal bleeding and pelvic pain: history, speculum examination and cervical biopsy, blood count and iron studies, conversion of opium tincture to measured oral morphine, an iron infusion, and a gynecologic oncology referral
Two-week follow-up and gynecologic oncology consultation: pathology, MRI and PET-CT, staging, treatment intent, palliative care, and long-acting morphine
Six-week review: bleeding and pain after palliative pelvic radiation, the first cycle of chemotherapy with pembrolizumab, blood counts, mood and opioid safety
Fourteen-week review: restaging CT, blood counts, iron and thyroid, pain, and a goals-of-care conversation
Twenty-week review after the last chemotherapy cycle: blood counts, thyroid on pembrolizumab, tapering morphine, mood and her work

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Gynecologic oncology consultation in two weeks for a friable cervical mass with bleeding and pain, biopsied today: diagnosis, staging, treatment intent, bleeding control, and pain

Stop opium tincture and change to measured oral morphine solution 5 mg every 4 hours as needed with an oral syringe, with acetaminophen, senna and polyethylene glycol, a naloxone nasal spray, a prescription monitoring check, locked storage, one prescriber, and review in two weeks
Iron deficiency anemia: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg intravenously today and in two weeks, with a blood count at each visit and ferritin 6 to 8 weeks after the infusions
Blood tests: blood count, ferritin, creatinine, ALT, albumin and a pregnancy test; HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests before any cancer treatment; PHQ-9

Staging by FIGO 1843 with pelvic MRI and PET-CT, and a CT-guided biopsy of a lung nodule; tumor PD-L1, mismatch repair and HER2 testing; no germline testing, because cervical cancer is not a hereditary cancer syndrome

Palliative pelvic radiation, 20 Gy in 5 fractions, for bleeding and pain, then carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab every 3 weeks for six cycles with pembrolizumab continuing, without bevacizumab while bleeding and after pelvic radiation; blood counts before each cycle and thyroid tests every six weeks

Specialist palliative care alongside cancer treatment from diagnosis, for pain, symptoms, mood, and goals-of-care conversations, with long-acting morphine 15 mg every 12 hours and oral morphine 5 mg as needed for breakthrough pain
Average pelvic pain at or below 3 of 10 without daytime sedation
Average pain 3 of 10 after radiation, on long-acting morphine, without daytime sleepiness
Bleeding controlled and hemoglobin above 10 g/dL without transfusion
No bleeding since radiation; hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL
A documented goals-of-care conversation and a named health care agent
Advance care plan and goals-of-care conversation recorded
Able to work on her mathematics for at least two hours most mornings

list.item: Independent in self-care; tires on stairs; ECOG performance status 1 [S]
